title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. With w = 1010110 and a = 10, the tape at a left extension during an active phase is 0 0 w^n ... a^k 1: each bounce adds one w at the left and removes one a from the right-end block. From step 302,136,397 to 2,126,686,397 the left counter goes 648 → 10648 while the right block goes 10159 → 159. When the block is used up the machine stops extending to the left for a long time (steps 2.17·109 to 3.85·109) and builds a new right block (6363 pairs) out of the middle of the tape, which is a hierarchy of repeated patterns ((a^2 w a^10 w)^m, (a^8 w a^40 w)^m, then a few large blocks). The sweeps are proved in Lean; the phase rule is observed, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 63,240 cells have been visited and 34,284 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.659). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.486).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text:
The head sweeps over long runs of a repeated word, rewriting each copy, for any number n of copies and any surrounding tape. Examples:
  • L A> (01)^n R → L (10)^n A> R
  • L (01)^n B> 0 R → L B> 0 (01)^n R
  • L B> (10)^n R → L (01)^n B> R
  • L (10)^n C> 1 R → L C> 1 (10)^n R
Generated by py/rules.py (tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: Draining phases
claims.text: At left extensions from step 302,136,397 the tape ends ... w^n 1 a^k w with (n, k) = (648, 10159), (1048, 9759), ..., (10648, 159): n + k stays 10807 and one bounce moves one unit. A later phase starts at step 3,847,811,442 with a block of 6363 and drains the same way (n + k = 16925).

claims.title: Rebuild phases
claims.text: Between active phases the head stays away from the left end: steps 39.6·10<sup>6</sup> to 295.8·10<sup>6</sup> and 2.17·10<sup>9</sup> to 3.85·10<sup>9</sup>. The active phases started at steps 24.4·10<sup>6</sup> (block 569), 295.8·10<sup>6</sup> (10236) and 3.85·10<sup>9</sup> (6363).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 63,240 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A bouncer that drains a block
html: Write w for 1010110 and a for 10. In an active phase the head bounces between the two ends; the tape is a counter w^n at the left, a middle part, and a block a^k at the right. Each bounce moves one unit: n grows by one and k drops by one. From step 302,136,397 to 2,126,686,397, (n, k) goes from (648, 10159) to (10648, 159).

sections.heading: Rebuilding the block
html: The middle part is hierarchical: long stretches of a^2 w a^10 w, then a^8 w a^40 w (four times as large), then a handful of large blocks (21, 333, 922, 530, 2289, ...). When the right block is used up, the head stays in the middle and right for a long time and builds the next right block out of this part (6363 pairs at step 3.85·109). Each rebuild takes longer. A halt (F reading 1) would have to happen during a rebuild; the rebuild rule is not written down.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.659). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.486).
After 109 steps the tape spans 63,240 cells (9,111 left of the start, 39,355 right), with a density of 1s of 0.542.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Alternating phases. In an active phase the head bounces across the whole tape; each bounce turns one pair 10 of the right-end block into one more word 1010110 at the left. When the right-end block is used up, a long reorganization rebuilds a new one from a hierarchical middle part. Halting open.
family: bouncer with a draining block and rebuilds
